subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Tesla's Founding
description: Learn Tesla's Founding in one minute.

hook.text: Tesla was founded in 2003 by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning—not by Elon Musk.

buildup.text: They believed lithium-ion batteries had finally reached the point where a practical EV was possible.

discovery.text: Their plan: start with an expensive sports car, use profits to fund cheaper models over time.

twist.text: Musk joined as lead investor and chairman in 2004. He later became CEO after internal conflicts.

climax.text: The strategy worked. Roadster funded Model S, which funded Model 3—each cheaper and higher volume.

punchline.text: Tesla's master plan was public from the start.

details.summary: Tesla was founded in 2003 by Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning, with Elon Musk joining as chairman and lead investor shortly after, aiming to prove that electric cars could be fast, desirable, and practical.
details.whyItMatters: Tesla's founding challenged a century of automaker assumptions that EVs were impractical. Its success forced the entire automotive industry to take electrification seriously and invest accordingly.
takeaways: Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning co-founded Tesla in 2003
Elon Musk led the Series A funding round and became chairman
The company's strategy was to start luxury and scale down in price

faq.question: Did Elon Musk actually found Tesla?
faq.answer: No. Martin Eberhard and Marc Tarpenning incorporated Tesla Motors in July 2003. Musk joined as chairman and largest shareholder through his Series A investment in 2004. A legal settlement later allowed all five early members to call themselves co-founders.

faq.question: What was Tesla's original business strategy?
faq.answer: Start with an expensive sports car to prove EVs could be desirable, use those profits to build a more affordable sedan, then use sedan profits to build a mass-market car. This top-down approach is known as Tesla's master plan.
